audit.whatIsWrong: Row 6 disagrees with the packet chart and with the page's own text. Packet has Tryndamere at 2+ items; both layers hold Riven.
audit.why: content.late opens 'Past two items this lane goes to Tryndamere' and whys[6] says to stop taking 1v1 duels — under win[6]=Riven. The remaining six rows already match the packet.
audit.corrected: Row 6 -> Tryndamere in both layers, rating 5/10 -> 3/10, phases[6].why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid states 'His R sits at roughly 160 seconds early and around 100 at rank 3'. Undying Rage is 120/100/80 — the rank-1 figure is overstated by 40 seconds and the rank-3 figure is overstated by 20.
audit.why: This is the number the entire page is built on: every all-in decision is gated on whether Undying Rage is up. A player counting to 160 will hold their combo through a window that opened 40 seconds earlier, and one expecting 100 at rank 3 will walk into an R that came back at 80.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 120 at rank 1 and 80 at rank 3 in content.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout does not appear anywhere on the page — not in the seven phases, the breakdowns, the do's, the don'ts, or any content field.
audit.why: It is the ability that punishes the exact play the page tells you to make. Riot's W text: it decreases surrounding champions' ATTACK DAMAGE, and 'Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' The page's core loop ends 'E out before he retaliates' — turning your back is precisely what arms the slow, and the AD cut lands mid-combo on a champion whose damage is all AD. It is 850 range on 14 seconds, so he can apply it before you are even in your own 275-range Q.
audit.corrected: Written into content.mid with its range, cooldown and the back-turned condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] and content.late frame Tryndamere's late-game threat as 'sustained auto DPS and Bloodlust healing', missing the mechanic that actually makes him unkillable in a bruiser duel.
audit.why: Riot's Q text: 'Tryndamere thrives on the thrills of combat, increasing his Attack Damage as he is more and more wounded.' The lower he gets, the harder he hits — so the standard Riven plan of chunking him toward an execute is also the plan that maximises his damage. That is why chip-then-finish fails here and one clean burst window does not.
audit.corrected: whys[6] rewritten onto the wounded-scaling AD.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text names 'Phantom Drive' as a Tryndamere item. No such item exists — it conflates Phantom Dancer with Trinity Force's Phantom-adjacent naming.
audit.why: Same corruption class the teemo mirror flagged with 'Liandry's Angueur'. A fabricated item name on a build recommendation is directly actionable and directly wrong.
audit.corrected: Corrected to Phantom Dancer, with Spinning Slash's rank-5 cooldown added in the same space.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are about tracking Undying Rage. His R sits at roughly 160 seconds early and around 100 at rank 3 — you should be tallying every time he burns it and only committing full combos when it is down, because if you dump everything into him and he pops R, you are standing next to a spinning crit machine with your own cooldowns on the floor. At level 6 the dynamic shifts back your way: Blade of the Exile lets you threaten him from range with empowered Q casts before closing, and Wind Slash is the counter to his R — shove him to low HP with the full combo, let the 5 seconds tick while you back off minimally, then throw Wind Slash the instant invulnerability expires for the execute. Do not burn Wind Slash early in the fight or you lose the kill.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are about tracking Undying Rage. It is 120 seconds at rank 1 and 80 at rank 3 — tally every time he burns it and commit full combos only when it is down, because if you dump everything into him and he pops R you are standing next to a spinning crit machine with your own cooldowns on the floor. Mocking Shout is the other tax: 850 range on 14 seconds, it cuts your attack damage and slows you whenever your back is turned, so the E-out that ends your combo is exactly when it bites hardest. At 6 the dynamic shifts back: Blade of the Exile threatens from range with empowered Q casts, and Wind Slash answers his R — burst him low, let the invulnerability tick, then throw the cone the instant it expires. Never spend Wind Slash early.

edits.before: Stack Bloodlust Q fury passively and hit a full-fury Spinning Slash to proc high-crit burst at the start of every trade
edits.after: Stack Battle Fury for crit chance, then open from 650 range with Spinning Slash so his crit autos land before your stun does
